title: Sales Administrator
description:
Sales Administrator

Putney

Monday to Friday

£30-40k basic DOE

An organised and proactive Sales Administrator is required to support a busy residential sales and lettings office in Putney. This role is ideal for someone with strong administrative skills who enjoys working in a fast-paced, customer-focused property environment.

The successful Sales Administrator candidate will provide essential support to the sales and lettings team, helping to ensure the smooth running of daily operations.

As a Sales Administrator you will liaise with clients and contractors, prepare property documentation, manage enquiries, maintain accurate records, and contribute to delivering a professional and efficient service at every stage of the property process.

The Company:
- Independent residential sales and lettings agency
- Strong reputation within the local property market
- Professional, customer-focused and team-oriented culture

Key Responsibilities as a Sales Administrator:
- Providing administrative support to the sales and lettings teams
- Preparing property details, correspondence and marketing materials
- Managing telephone, email and office enquiries efficiently
- Updating property records and maintaining database accuracy
- Liaising with clients, solicitors, contractors and third parties
- Supporting sales and lettings progression while maintaining office systems

title: Interim HR Coordinator, 2 months
description:
Interim HR Coordinator, 2 months - East London - Leading FE College - £20 per hour (Umbrella)

4 days on site

This is an exciting opportunity for an immediately available HR Coordinator to join a leading FE College based in East London.

Reporting into an HR Business Partner you will be responsible for providing a proactive and efficient HR administration service. Your key accountabilities will include:-
- Assisting with embedding HR policies and procedures across the College
- Providing first line advice and guidance to managers on a range of employment issues
- Supporting the HR Business Partner with employee relations cases and with recruitment
- Working in partnership with managers to ensure all HR and Recruitment documentation are completed accurately
- Taking ownership of administrative changes
- Managing the HR inbox in a timely manner
- Ensuring the Single Central Record is fully compliant
- Providing support for the full recruitment cycle
- Maintaining the HR system

You should be an HR Coordinator or HR Administrator with experience of HR, Payroll and Recruitment administration ideally gained in the Education sector. Experience of working with HR Systems (preferably I-Trent) needs to be combined with a proven ability to provide guidance on policies and processes. Maths and English at GCSE level 4 is essential. It is also essential that you have excellent organisational skills and are able to multitask.

Morgan Hunt is a multi-award-winning recruitment Business for interim, contract and temporary recruitment and acts as an Employment Agency in relation to temporary vacancies. Morgan Hunt is an equal opportunities employer, job suitability are assessed on merit in accordance with their skills, qualifications and abilities to perform the relevant duties required in a particular role.

title: Marketing Planner
description:
Marketing Planner - Premium Brand
£30,000pa - £40,000pa + Company Benefits
London

A prestigious premium brand renowned for its innovative performance accessories and equipment collections is currently recruiting for a Marketing Planner to join its growing Head Office team in London.

This is a fantastic opportunity for an experienced Marketing professional to take ownership of the brand's planning and coordination across marketing, events and partnerships end-to-end, while managing the marketing calendar and go-to-market plan across the business.

Working closely with the CEO and managing the Creative Lead, the Marketing Manager will play a pivotal role in protecting and building the brand's position as the world's most recognisable luxury motorcycle helmet brand.

The Role:
- Own and manage the annual marketing calendar and go-to-market plan, aligning product launches, campaigns, events and channel activity throughout the year.
- Define and deliver integrated marketing campaigns and customer acquisition activity across all relevant channels, tracking and reporting performance against agreed KPIs.
- Protect and develop the brand's luxury positioning, tone of voice and visual identity across every customer touchpoint.
- Own the events and partnerships strategy end-to-end, including defining and delivering the annual events calendar, organising and attending events, and managing brand partnerships and activations.
- Lead PR and press strategy and execution, while managing ambassador and talent relationships.
- Drive brand collaborations with partners both within and outside of the motorcycle industry, working closely with the CEO.
- Manage the Creative Lead and oversee content output, directing the editing and delivery of creative assets to the Digital Team in line with the overall brand direction.
- Organise lifestyle shoots and product content
- Coordinate trade show presence and work closely with the Digital Team and CEO.

In return, you will have the opportunity to join a highly respected and growing premium brand, offering excellent career progression, broad product exposure and a competitive salary and benefits package.

title: Temp HR Coordinator - Media
description:
We're looking for a highly organised and detail-focused HR Coordinator to join a busy International HR team in West London.

This is a hands-on role supporting the smooth running of the HR function, with a particular focus on HR administration, payroll, HR systems and reporting. You'll be responsible for keeping employee data accurate, coordinating starters and leavers, preparing HR documentation and supporting payroll across multiple countries.

There's a big freelance population you will support, predominantly with issuing contracts and supporting with documentation as well as tracking activity and data.

Reporting into the HRD, you will provide day-to-day support to employees and managers and be their first point of contact for queries. There will also be opportunities to get involved in wider HR projects and process improvements.

We're looking for someone with solid HR administration experience who is confident working with HR systems, spreadsheets and data. You'll be highly organised, comfortable juggling priorities and have a real eye for detail - someone who likes getting things right first time and is happy to get stuck in.

The role is based in West London and requires 4 days a week on site, paid on a daily rate equivalent to £35-38k annual salary DOE.

If you are immediately available, and want to hear more - please apply now!

title: Ebilling Coordinator
description:
As an E-billing Coordinator in London, you'll manage the day-to-day electronic billing processes to ensure smooth and accurate invoicing within the professional services industry. Your role will involve working closely with internal teams and external stakeholders to support the accounting and finance department.

Client Details

A leading global law firm based in London.

Description
- Oversee and maintain the electronic billing system for accuracy and efficiency.
- Coordinate with clients and internal teams to resolve billing discrepancies.
- Ensure compliance with client-specific billing requirements and guidelines.
- Prepare and submit invoices through various electronic billing platforms.
- Monitor and manage billing deadlines to ensure timely submissions.
- Generate and analyse billing reports to identify and address issues promptly.
- Maintain accurate records of all billing activities and communications.
- Provide support and training to internal stakeholders on e-billing processes.

Profile

A successful E-billing Coordinator should have:
- Experience with electronic billing systems and processes.
- Knowledge of accounting and finance principles within professional services.
- Strong organisational skills and attention to detail.
- Excellent communication and problem-solving abilities.
- The ability to work collaboratively with internal and external stakeholders.
- Proficiency in relevant software and billing platforms.

Job Offer
- Salary ranging from £36,000 to £54,000, dependent on the level of experience.
- Private medical insurance.
- Access to a free in-house fitness centre and subsidised health club memberships.
- Free onsite GP service and periodic health assessments.
- Pension and flexible savings options.
- Income protection and life assurance.

If you're interested in this role, apply now.

title: Business Support Officer
description:
Job title: Acturis Support Officer

Location: London (hybrid working available)

Salary: negotiable

Job Purpose:

A support person with a good level of insurance and operational knowledge with a focus on Acturis to provide first line support for businesses in relation to their broking systems either by email or phone.

Support the business to resolve specific issues or proactively propose further developments or changes to address common problems.

Working with the Acturis Support Lead to provide effective and timely remote or on-site support for users in accordance with current priorities.

Operating in a new Retail Operations team, this is an opportunity to provide essential support to the businesses across the UK delivering to the Retail Strategy and Core Values.

THIS ROLE REQUIRES EXPERIENCE WITH THE ACTURIS SYSTEM, AS WELL AS INSURANCE KNOWLEDGE. APPLICATIONS WITHOUT THIS EXPERIENCE WILL NOT BE CONSIDERED.

Responsibilities:
- To assist the Acturis Support Lead to deliver support and assistance to the business
- Liaise with third parties including Acturis to ensure issues or change requests are resolved promptly and accurately
- Work with the Acturis Support Lead and Senior Business Support Officers to facilitate configuration changes to the various Acturis environments including documentation, as well as the necessary support required for migrations.
- Provide on-site support for new groups of users of Acturis
- Working with the Acturis Support Lead to identify opportunities for improvement or change in configuration or functionality

Principal Accountabilities / Responsibilities:
- Resolution of business queries and issues
- Adherence to required SLA's
- Adhere to Acturis Change Board controls and requirements.

description:

An exciting opportunity has arisen for an experienced Credit Controller to join the finance team of a rapidly expanding international business based in Central London.

This is a varied credit control position within a commercially focused organisation where you'll have responsibility for a diverse customer ledger and work closely with colleagues across Finance, Sales and Operations.

The role would suit an experienced Credit Controller who enjoys having ownership of their accounts, building strong customer relationships and taking a proactive approach to recovering outstanding payments. NetSuite experience is highly desirable, as you'll be using the system regularly to monitor accounts, review balances and maintain accurate financial information.

About the Role:

As Credit Controller, you'll be responsible for keeping customer accounts up to date and ensuring outstanding invoices are followed up effectively.

You'll take a structured approach to your ledger, identifying overdue accounts, investigating issues and agreeing payment solutions with customers. You'll also work closely with internal departments where billing, contractual or account queries are preventing payment.

Experience dealing with complicated invoices, underpayments and legacy payments will be very beneficial. Further experience conducting investigations into aged debt and outstanding invoices will be very a great asset for this credit control role.

There may also be opportunities to support finance and operational teams during major events, giving the role a broader commercial dimension than a traditional credit control position.

Key Duties:
- Take day-to-day responsibility for an allocated customer ledger.
- Monitor outstanding invoices and carry out regular collection activity.
- Contact customers by telephone and email to agree payment dates and resolve overdue balances.
- Review aged debt and determine appropriate follow-up actions.
- Maintain accurate notes and records of collection activity.
- Investigate account discrepancies, invoice queries and disputed balances.
- Produce customer statements and respond to account-related enquiries.
- Work with Sales and other departments to resolve issues affecting payment.
- Reconcile customer and sales information between internal systems and NetSuite.
- Help minimise aged debt, credit notes and unallocated cash.
- Ensure payments are chased ahead of key event and operational deadlines.
- Maintain accurate customer account information.
- Deal confidently with customers across different markets and currencies.
- Provide assistance to on-site teams with customer payments when required.

We're particularly interested in candidates who have:
- Solid Credit Control or Accounts Receivable experience.
- Previous experience using NetSuite.
- Good Excel skills.
- Experience dealing with multi-currency accounts and international customers.
- A good understanding of VAT and financial processes.
- Excellent communication and negotiation skills.
- The confidence to deal with customers regarding overdue payments.
- Strong attention to detail and numerical accuracy.
- Good organisation and the ability to prioritise a busy workload.
- A proactive approach to resolving problems rather than simply reporting them.
- Experience within events, exhibitions, media or another fast-moving commercial environment would be advantageous.

The Working Environment

The company has an informal and sociable culture, offering a refreshing alternative to a traditional corporate finance environment.

You'll be working in a relaxed office with a casual dress code, alongside a team that regularly gets together for social events, celebrations and nights out.

The business is continuing to grow internationally, so this is an opportunity to join a finance function where there is plenty of activity and exposure to different areas of the organisation.

Package:
- Salary: £34,000 - £36,000
- Location: Central London
- Hybrid: 3 days in the office / 2 days from home
- Start: Immediate
- Holiday: 25 days + 8 bank holidays
- Pension: Company pension scheme
- Additional benefits: Cycle to Work scheme and Season Ticket Loan

You will keep immaculate records in our case management system, provide timely updates, and collaborate with colleagues in property management and tech to refine processes and solve problems.

- You move RTM cases from instruction to acquisition smoothly, on time, and with minimal escalations.

- Clients feel informed and supported, with proactive updates and clear, jargon-free advice.

- You use technology to increase speed and quality, contributing ideas that improve templates and workflows.

- Conducting RTM eligibility checks, title reviews, and due diligence on buildings, leases, and tenant participation.
- Preparing, serving, and tracking statutory notices, including Notices of Invitation to Participate and Notices of Claim.
- Managing critical dates, responses, and counter-notices, and coordinating the acquisition process.
- Drafting correspondence and standard documents, and maintaining accurate file notes and document bundles.
- Liaising with leaseholders, RTM company directors, landlords, managing agents, and external advisors.
- Updating the case management system, generating reports, and refining templates and processes with our tech tools.

WHO THIS ROLE IS FOR
- You are detail-obsessed, organised, and comfortable running your own caseload with appropriate oversight.

- You stay calm under pressure, prioritise effectively, and keep multiple matters moving at pace.

- Drafting and serving statutory notices, and managing matter timelines and critical dates.
- Client-facing experience, balancing empathy with commercial pragmatism in written and verbal communications.
- Coordinating multi-stakeholder matters and preparing orderly, audit-ready legal files.

- Employee referral scheme, up to £1,500

We are on a mission to become the leading international force in residential property management. What we do matters to billions of people in their everyday lives.

Residential real estate is the world's largest asset class, and for most families, buying a home is the single biggest financial decision they will ever make. For too long, residential property management has fallen short of homeowners' and residents' expectations, and the industry is ready for change. Odevo was formed to make that change happen.

In just six years, Odevo has grown more than 70-fold, establishing us as the leading international player. title: Continuity of Care Coordinator
description:
Continuity of Care Coordinator

Location: Based primarily at HMP Brixton

Salary: £18,049.02 per annum

Vacancy Type: Permanent

About The Role

Are you passionate about improving outcomes for people leaving prison and making sure they receive the right support when they return to the community?

We're looking for an enthusiastic and organised Continuity of Care Coordinator to join our substance misuse team at HMP Brixton. This is an exciting opportunity to play a key role in strengthening the journey from prison into community treatment, building effective partnerships and helping ensure people leaving custody experience a safe and supported transition.

Based primarily at HMP Brixton, you'll work across our London services, including HMP Wormwood Scrubs and Heathrow IRC, so some travel will be required. Reasonable travel expenses will be covered.

What you will be doing

You'll be at the heart of improving continuity of care across our London prison services. Your responsibilities will include:
- Leading monthly release audits, ensuring service users are correctly discharged on NDTMS and that any data issues are identified and resolved.
- Completing pre-release audits to make sure community teams are fully informed and prepared for an individual's release.
- Ensuring alert forms and key information are shared with community services so that support can continue without unnecessary delays.
- Building strong relationships with local authority and community substance misuse teams, developing effective referral pathways and joint-working arrangements.
- Keeping up to date with local community treatment offers and ensuring prison teams have the information they need to support successful referrals.
- Establishing and chairing continuity of care forums, bringing partners together to identify challenges, share learning and improve outcomes.
- Producing accurate meeting minutes, actions and progress updates, ensuring agreed improvements are followed through.
- Acting as a key point of contact for community prison in-reach workers, helping them overcome barriers and supporting effective pre-release reviews.
- Leading regional NDTMS and other relevant audits, identifying opportunities to improve data quality and performance.
- Supporting the organisation of release fairs and events within the prison, helping service users connect with community support.
- Regularly reviewing and updating the Continuity of Care Best Practice Framework, ensuring it reflects current guidance and good practice.
- Developing strong community partnerships that improve continuity of care and outcomes for service users.
- Working collaboratively with Health and Justice colleagues, NHSE and OHID to support the delivery of commissioning projects and initiatives.
- Sharing best practice, progress and learning with managers and teams across the region.

What we are looking for

We're looking for someone who is passionate about partnership working and committed to making a real difference to people moving from prison back into the community.

You'll ideally bring:
- Experience of working within substance misuse, health, criminal justice or a related setting.
- A strong understanding of the challenges people can face when transitioning from prison into community services.
- Excellent communication and relationship-building skills, with the ability to work confidently with a wide range of partners.
- Strong organisational skills and the ability to manage audits, meetings, actions and deadlines effectively.
- Excellent attention to detail, particularly when working with data, records and performance information.
- The confidence to chair meetings, influence others and drive actions forward.

title: Commercial Real Estate Paralegal
description:
A well-established commercial law firm is seeking a Commercial Real Estate Paralegal to join its Harrow office. This is an excellent opportunity for a Commercial Real Estate Paralegal looking to build a long-term career within a respected property team, supporting experienced solicitors across a broad range of commercial property transactions. The successful Commercial Real Estate Paralegal will gain exposure to acquisitions, asset management, landlord and tenant matters, development work and banking transactions, with occasional travel to the firm's West End office when required.

The Company?

The successful Commercial Real Estate Paralegal will join an established law firm with a strong reputation across commercial real estate, banking and finance, property development, property litigation, landlord and tenant, and private client work. The team offers hands-on mentoring, quality work and clear opportunities to develop towards qualification.

The Role

As the Commercial Real Estate Paralegal you will support fee earners on a varied caseload of commercial property matters from instruction through to completion.

The role will include:

Drafting legal documents, reports and correspondence
Assisting with commercial real estate transactions and due diligence
Conducting Land Registry, Companies House and legal research
Preparing and submitting Land Registry and SDLT applications
Liaising with clients, solicitors, lenders and third parties
Managing file opening, compliance and AML procedures
Preparing bills, completion statements and transaction documents
Managing diaries, workflows and case management systems
Supporting fee earners with general administration and document production
Providing assistance across multiple teams when required

The Commercial Real Estate Paralegal?

You will be a proactive and organised individual with a genuine interest in commercial property law.

The Commercial Real Estate Paralegal must have:

LLB or GDL/PGDL qualification
At least one year's paralegal experience within a law firm
Commercial real estate, asset management or landlord and tenant experience would be advantageous
Ambition to qualify as a Solicitor in the future
Excellent written and verbal communication skills
Strong organisational skills and attention to detail
Ability to manage multiple priorities in a busy environment
Experience using Microsoft Office and legal case management systems
Professional and client-focused approach with strong teamwork skills

In return ?

£25,000 - £32,000 salary
High-quality commercial real estate work
Direct mentoring from experienced property solicitors
Exposure to acquisitions, development, landlord and tenant and asset management matters
Ongoing training and career development
Harrow office location with occasional travel to the West End office
Genuine long-term progression opportunities

If you are a Commercial Real Estate Paralegal considering your next career move, please contact Chris van Aurich at Brandon James on for a confidential discussion.

title: Court & Warrant Administrator
description:
Are you highly organised, able to manage multiple tasks at once, and enjoy working in a fast-paced operational environment? Do you thrive on delivering excellent service, coordinating workloads, and working closely with colleagues, clients, and field teams to achieve shared goals?

Due to company growth, we are looking for a Court & Warrant Team Administrator to join our Operations team based in Romford.

Purpose of the Role

Reporting to the Operations Manager, you will play a key role within our Court & Warrant team, helping to deliver excellent service to both Richburns and our clients. Working from our Romford office, you will support our field agents and operational teams by coordinating workloads, managing appointments, processing documentation, and ensuring services are delivered efficiently and within agreed timescales.

This role requires strong organisational skills, attention to detail, and the ability to manage competing priorities. You will work closely with internal departments, clients, field agents, courts, and third-party suppliers while contributing to both company and client-led KPIs.

- Manage the diaries and workloads of field agents to ensure work is completed efficiently and in line with operational requirements.

- Attend court hearings to obtain Warrants of Entry when required.
- Support colleagues by providing cover during periods of absence to ensure consistent service delivery.
- Build and maintain strong working relationships with clients, suppliers, field staff, and internal teams.

The above is not an exhaustive list and other duties may be required.

Why work at Richburns?

You will be part of a successful and rapidly growing company, with an open and supportive environment. Some other benefits include:
- Employee assistance programme
- Death in Service benefit
- 25 days holiday (pro-rated for part time) plus 8 days bank holidays
- 3% pension
- Personal and career development opportunities

You must not have a criminal record and will be required to undergo a DBS check (Disclosure and Barring Service) and Credit Reference Check.

- Working with nominal ledgers and ensuring transactions are correctly allocated
- Liaising directly with clients to obtain information and resolve queries

- Dealing with ad hoc bookkeeping and client queries
- Assisting with occasional secretarial and administrative matters where required

About You

We're looking for someone with a minimum of two years' bookkeeping experience who is confident managing their own workload and communicating directly with clients.

Ideally, you will have:
- A minimum of 2 years' bookkeeping experience
- Previous experience working within an accountancy firm or practice would be ideal

- A good understanding of bookkeeping and accounting principles
- Experience using bookkeeping and accounting software

- Experience preparing VAT returns
- Experience processing and reconciling bank transactions
- Experience preparing and posting manual journals
- A good understanding of nominal ledgers
- Excellent attention to detail and a high level of accuracy
- Good organisational and time-management skills
- The ability to work independently and meet deadlines
- Confidence communicating and liaising directly with clients
- A friendly, reliable and flexible approach

Experience of managing bookkeeping for a number of different clients within an accountancy practice environment would be particularly advantageous.

What We Offer
- Part-time - 3 days per week

- Thereafter: flexible hybrid working with a minimum of 1 day per week in the office
- The option to work additional days in the office if preferred
- Occasional additional office attendance where required for projects, client requirements or business needs
- A friendly and supportive working environment
- A varied role working with a range of clients and accounting software

title: HR Assistant
description:
HR Assistant
Up to £32,000 DOE plus benefits
North Nottinghamshire
Predominantly onsite, with ad-hoc WFH available (typically once a week)
Permanent & Full Time

Are you looking for an HR role where you can get involved in far more than just HR administration?

This is a brilliant opportunity for an HR Assistant to join a busy, hands-on HR function within a fast-paced environment. You'll be working closely with the wider business and gaining exposure across the employee lifecycle, making this a great next step for someone looking to continue building their HR career. It's a genuinely varied position. One day you could be supporting with payroll and updating employee records, the next preparing documentation for an employee relations case, producing people reports or helping coordinate an employee engagement initiative.

The role will include:
- Providing day-to-day HR administration and support to employees and managers
- Maintaining accurate employee records and updating HR systems
- Preparing HR letters, documentation and employee correspondence
- Supporting monthly payroll administration and employee changes
- Managing sickness, absence and holiday records
- Supporting disciplinary and investigation processes, including preparing documentation and taking meeting notes
- Producing HR reports, people data and management information
- Supporting recruitment, onboarding and wider employee lifecycle activity
- Assisting with probation, performance and appraisal processes
- Supporting the development and implementation of HR policies and processes
- Coordinating training, employee engagement, wellbeing and recognition activities
- Responding to general HR queries and supporting the wider HR team

We're looking for someone who is organised, proactive and genuinely interested in continuing to develop their career within HR. You'll need strong attention to detail, confidence working with systems and data, and the ability to build good relationships with people across the business. Sadly, this one can't be your first role within HR. We do need someone who already has some previous HR administration experience and understands the basics of working within a busy HR function.
You certainly don't need to know everything, though! Just as importantly, we're looking for someone who is keen to learn, happy to get involved and excited by the opportunity to broaden their experience and continue developing their HR knowledge.

If you're currently working within HR and feel ready for a role that will give you broader exposure and plenty of opportunity to develop, I'd love to hear from you.

title: Legal Services Administrator
company: South London and Maudsley NHS Foundation Trust
advertiser_name: South London and Maudsley NHS Foundation Trust
description: Are you an organised, proactive administrator looking for an opportunity to develop your career within NHS Legal Services? South London and Maudsley NHS Foundation Trust is looking for an enthusiastic and highly organised Legal Services Administrator to join our busy and supportive Legal Services team. This is a varied role providing administrative and coordination support across a broad range of legal matters, including claims, inquests and Court of Protection matters. You will be an important part of the Legal Services team, helping to ensure that legal matters are managed efficiently, accurately and within required timescales. You will work closely with Legal Services Officer, the Legal Services Manager and colleagues across the Trust. This role would suit someone who enjoys working in a busy environment, takes pride in getting the detail right and is confident dealing with confidential and sometimes sensitive information. You do not need to be a qualified legal professional. We are looking for someone with strong administrative skills, excellent organisation and attention to detail, and an interest in developing their knowledge and experience of NHS Legal Services. You will provide administrative support to the Legal Services team, helping to keep cases, documents and deadlines organised and ensuring that colleagues have the information and support they need. Acting as a first point of contact for routine enquiries to Legal Services and ensuring these are logged, acknowledged and directed appropriately. Maintaining accurate legal case records, databases, trackers and case management systems. Tracking key deadlines, hearings and actions and ensuring records are kept up to date. Supporting the collation of clinical records, policies and other information required for legal matters and disclosure. Assisting with the preparation and collation of legal documents, correspondence, witness statements and evidence bundles. Arranging meetings, case conferences, hearings, calls and witness meetings. Preparing routine correspondence, reports and meeting papers. Liaising with clinical and corporate teams to obtain information and documentation. Communicating professionally and sensitively with staff, patients, families, external solicitors, Coroner's Officers and other agencies. Handling confidential and sensitive information appropriately and in accordance with information governance requirements. Recognising urgent, complex or sensitive matters and escalating them appropriately. Providing general administrative support to the Legal Services team. The postholder will provide comprehensive administrative and coordination support to the Trusts Legal Services function. You will work within agreed processes and procedures, using your initiative to manage your workload and ensure that administrative tasks are completed accurately and within required timescales. You will be expected to recognise when a matter is urgent, complex or sensitive and escalate it to an appropriate member of the Legal Services team. What you will bring Highly organised, with the ability to manage competing priorities and deadlines. Accurate and attentive to detail. Confident using IT systems, including Microsoft Office, Outlook, Word, Excel and databases. Able to maintain accurate records and ensure information is filed and retrievable. A clear and professional communicator, both verbally and in writing. Comfortable working with confidential and sensitive information. Able to work calmly and professionally under pressure. Proactive and able to work independently within defined procedures. A positive team player who is willing to support colleagues and contribute to an efficient and supportive Legal Services function. You will have experience of providing administrative support in a busy office environment, maintaining records or databases, preparing correspondence and documents, arranging meetings and dealing with internal and external stakeholders. Experience of managing competing priorities and deadlines is also important. Experience of working within an NHS, healthcare, legal, governance, claims, complaints, risk or regulatory environment would be advantageous. An awareness of inquests, claims, Court of Protection or Mental Capacity Act processes would also be desirable. You will be educated to A-level standard or have equivalent experience, with GCSE English and Maths or equivalent. A legal secretary, paralegal, CILEX, business administration or healthcare administration qualification would be desirable. Why this role? This is an excellent opportunity for an experienced administrator who wants to develop their skills within a specialist NHS environment. You will gain exposure to a wide variety of legal matters and will work alongside experienced legal professionals while developing your understanding of the processes and governance that underpin NHS Legal Services. If you are organised, approachable and motivated to make a difference, and you are looking for a role where your administrative skills will have a direct impact on the effective delivery of an important Trust function, we would love to hear from you.

You will be dealing with patients face-to-face and over the telephone, supporting appointments and enquiries, processing administrative work and working closely with our clinical and administrative teams. It can be demanding, but it is also extremely rewarding. Every day you will have the opportunity to make a genuine difference to someone's experience of the NHS whether that is helping a patient navigate the practice, resolving a problem, or simply providing a friendly and reassuring point of contact. We value teamwork, kindness, reliability and a willingness to learn. In return, you will join a close-knit team where your contribution matters and where every member of staff plays an important part in delivering a high-quality service to our patients. If you enjoy working with people, thrive in a busy environment and want a role where no two days are the same, we would love to hear from you. Previous GP or NHS experience is desirable, but full training will be provided. We will only contact candidates who are shortlisted for interview. If invited you will be required to complete a typing test. We are seeking a part-time, permanent Patient Administrator to join our amazing team. Hours: 16.5 hours over 3 days Monday: 1:00pm - 6:00pm Wednesday: 1:00pm - 6:45pm Friday: 1:00pm - 6:45pm Brief Description of Duties As a Patient Administrator, you will be one of the first points of contact for our patients and will play an important role in helping them access the right service at the right time. Your duties will include: Welcoming and assisting patients at reception in a friendly and professional manner. Answering telephone calls and responding to patient enquiries. Supporting patients with appointments and directing them to the most appropriate service or member of the team. Responding to emails and online enquiries, including our online triage system. Processing repeat prescription requests and dealing with prescription-related administrative queries. Undertaking DOCMAN administration, including scanning, coding and filing incoming. Filing and maintaining patient records and ensuring information is processed accurately and promptly. Completing general administrative tasks to support the smooth running of the practice. Liaising with clinical and non-clinical teams. Handling confidential and sensitive information in accordance with practice policies and NHS requirements. Current patients of the Surgery: If you are offered this position, you would need to register with another GP practice before commencing employment with us. RESPONSIBILITIES To provide a friendly, professional and helpful first point of contact for patients and visitors to the Surgery. To deal with patients by telephone, face-to-face, email and through the Practice's online triage system. To assist patients with appointments, queries and requests and direct them to the appropriate service, clinician or member of the Practice team. To undertake a range of reception and administrative duties to support the smooth and effective running of the Practice. To process patient information and administrative work accurately and in accordance with Practice protocols. To maintain patient confidentiality and comply with information governance and data protection requirements. To work collaboratively with both clinical and administrative colleagues. To remain calm, professional, helpful and courteous when dealing with patients, including during challenging or difficult interactions. TASKS TELEPHONE To log in to the Practice telephony system and respond to telephone calls as quickly and effectively as possible. To deal with, transfer or escalate calls as appropriate, following Practice protocols. To accept, record and transmit information accurately using EMIS, online triage system, generic email and other Practice computer systems. To assist patients with queries, requests and access to appropriate services. To provide a professional, calm and courteous service, including when dealing with challenging or difficult telephone interactions. To maintain confidentiality when discussing patient information over the telephone. To log out of the telephony system at the end of each working session. RECEPTION To receive patients and visitors arriving at the Practice in a welcoming, friendly and professional manner. To assist with patient queries and requests or pass messages to the appropriate person. To confidently navigate patient records using EMIS, Docman and other Practice systems in order to assist with patient queries. To make appointments for patients with the appropriate Practice service using EMIS, where required. To assist patients with the Practice's online triage system, including explaining how to access and use the service and directing patients to the appropriate route where required. To handle queries and requests for information or services and ensure that they are dealt with appropriately or transferred to a GP, healthcare professional, member of staff or outside agency in accordance with Practice protocols. To respond appropriately to patient queries received through generic email and other electronic communication channels, ensuring enquiries are dealt with or passed to the appropriate person. To maintain a professional and courteous approach at all times, including when dealing with challenging situations. ADMINISTRATION To undertake general administrative duties required for the smooth running of the Practice. To process repeat prescription requests and deal with prescription-related administrative queries in accordance with Practice protocols. To undertake DOCMAN administration, including receiving, scanning, attaching, coding and filing correspondence accurately into the correct patient's medical record and routing correspondence to the appropriate clinician or team. To process incoming hospital letters, clinic correspondence and other clinical documentation, ensuring that information is accurately recorded and reaches the appropriate clinician or member of the Practice team. To undertake general filing and maintain accurate and appropriately organised patient records. To respond to patient emails and electronic enquiries appropriately and within Practice protocols. To undertake administrative work relating to QOF call and recall lists when required. To assist with deductions from the Practice patient list/records in accordance with Practice procedures and guidance. To assist with administrative backlogs and other Practice administrative work as required. To accurately enter, update and maintain patient information using EMIS, Docman, online triage system and other Practice systems. To ensure that all patient information is handled securely and confidentially and in accordance with Practice policies, information governance requirements and data protection legislation. GENERAL To assist as required during periods of staff holiday, sickness, increased workload or other operational requirements. To work collaboratively with clinical and administrative colleagues, supporting one another and contributing positively to the wider Practice team. To undertake any other reasonable duties appropriate to the role as requested by the Practice Manager or Partners. To attend and complete Practice training and develop the knowledge and skills required for the role. Full training will be provided on Practice systems, including EMIS, Docman, online triage system and relevant Practice processes and protocols. To follow all Practice policies, procedures and protocols and raise any concerns with the Practice Manager. To maintain a professional, respectful, helpful and courteous approach towards patients, colleagues and other healthcare professionals. To remain calm and professional when dealing with challenging situations and seek assistance from an appropriate colleague where necessary. To contribute to the Practice's commitment to providing safe, compassionate and high-quality care to patients. To maintain confidentiality at all times and not disclose patient or Practice information except in accordance with Practice procedures and relevant legislation.

Process repeat prescription requests and route incoming clinical mail, workflow tasks, and results efficiently to the medical team. title: Medical Receptionist
description: Fernlea Surgery, is a busy and well-establish GP Practice in South Tottenham, North London, is seeking an enthusiastic Medical Receptionist/Administrator to join our friendly and supportive Medical Administration team. We have an excellent team of GPs and Nurses, a supportive Management Team and efficient administrative team. Our Practice list size is approximately 12,500. We are open to full time and part time applicants and can offer a range of shifts between Monday to Friday. Shifts would range from 8am - 6:30pm with either a 8am start or 1pm. What we offer A competitive salary Paid 30 minute lunch break per day NHS Pension scheme Paid DBS Starting with 20 days annual leave (plus bank holidays) Free on-site car parking Supportive and welcoming team environment Full training and development opportunities Main duties of the job This is a varied, rewarding position in a busy GP practice setting. The Medical Receptionist/Administrator will work across both administrative and reception functions within the practice, providing reliable operational support to clinicians and the wider multidisciplinary team. The role requires an individual who can work confidently with clinical systems, manage competing priorities, and provide a professional patient-facing service while exercising judgement and initiative. Job responsibilities Main duties and responsibilities of the post 1. Administrative and coordination responsibilities Undertake a broad range of administrative duties to support the effective running of the practice Process patient information (electronic and hard copy) accurately, securely, and in a timely manner Monitor, manage, and action incoming emails, electronic tasks, and workflow requests independently Carry out searches, audits, recalls, and administrative reporting as required Type letters, reports, referrals, and associated clinical documentation Respond to administrative requests from clinicians, using judgement to prioritise actions Identify system issues, workflow gaps, or risks and escalate appropriately Report faults to software suppliers and/or IT support and track progress 2. Reception and patient-facing responsibilities Act as a professional and confident point of contact for patients, both face to face and via telephone Respond to patient enquiries using judgement to prioritise urgent, complex, or sensitive matters Support safe navigation of patients to the most appropriate service in line with practice policy Book appointments, recalls, and follow-ups accurately using the computerised appointment system Monitor patient flow and waiting times and escalate concerns appropriately Explain practice procedures, registration processes, and temporary resident arrangements clearly 3. Clinical systems and medical records Assist with the accurate input, updating, and maintenance of patient records on EMIS Clinically code data and correspondence where appropriate Scan, upload, and file patient-related documentation promptly Open, date-stamp, and distribute correspondence, reports, and results to relevant clinicians Arrange retrieval, transfer, and re-filing of medical records as required 4. Communication and telephone systems Receive and make telephone calls in accordance with practice policy, using clear communication and active listening Take accurate messages and ensure timely communication with clinicians and team members Ensure the telephone system is operational at the start of each day and switched to night service at the end of the day 5. Start and end of day procedures Open the premises at the start of the day, deactivate alarms, and prepare the practice to receive patients Secure the premises at the end of the day, ensuring the building is locked and alarms activated Be able to work shifts between 8.00am and 6.30pm as required 6. Professional responsibilities Maintain strict confidentiality at all times Demonstrate the ability to think independently, problem-solve, and manage competing priorities Use initiative, discretion, and common sense when responding to patient and operational issues Communicate effectively with colleagues, clinicians, and external organisations Maintain a clean, organised, and efficient working environment Communicate and work collaboratively with colleagues at all levels, treating others with professionalism, courtesy, and respect at all times. 7. Additional duties Undertake any other delegated duties appropriate to the role This job description outlines the main duties of the post and may be reviewed and amended in line with service needs.

title: Patient Services Advisor/receptionist
description: Are you an experienced Receptionist/Administrative assistant or someone with transferrable skills who is good with people and can balance a varying workload? The Reception teams across Groves Health are the lynchpin of our business and support the Group to provide a first class service to our patients and the wider community. The role:- This is a varied role which will give you the opportunity to have exposure to different parts of Reception/Administration on a rotating basis within a busy GP surgery. Some of your duties will include:- Booking telephone appointments with patients Managing the incoming email inbox and patient requests Responding to patient queries via the Practice website dashboard Greeting patients when they arrive in the Practice and dealing with queries Calling patients on behalf of GP's to book appointments and relay information Managing incoming mail and distributing/scanning accordingly On occasion opening and closing the Practice Working with outside agencies such as Pharmacies and Care homes for patient care Registering new patients Using Practice software such as EMIS, Docman (training provided) and Office products Groves Health is a successful and trusted provider of NHS services across England. Over the past five years, we have grown from a single practice in New Malden to a team of more than 100 people, providing high-quality care to patients and communities across our four sites in New Malden, Richmond, Wimbledon and Hinchley Wood. As Groves Health continues to grow and expand the services we provide, we are looking for an enthusiastic and reliable Receptionist & Administrator to join our team at Groves Vineyard Surgery in Wimbledon . We are looking for someone who enjoys working with people, is well organised and can manage a varied workload in a busy environment. Previous experience in a GP practice, healthcare or administrative setting would be beneficial, but we are also keen to hear from candidates with transferable skills and a strong commitment to providing excellent customer service. Our Reception teams play a vital role in the day-to-day running of our practices. As one of the first points of contact for patients, you will help ensure that patients receive a friendly, professional and efficient service. This is a varied role, providing the opportunity to develop your knowledge and experience across different areas of reception and administration within a busy GP surgery. Your duties will include, but are not limited to: Booking and managing telephone appointments for patients. Managing the practice email inbox and responding to patient requests. Responding to patient queries through the practice website and online services. Welcoming patients to the practice and dealing with their queries in a professional and helpful manner. Contacting patients on behalf of GPs and other members of the clinical team to arrange appointments or relay information. Receiving, sorting, scanning and distributing incoming post and correspondence. Registering new patients and ensuring their information is accurately recorded. Liaising with external organisations, including pharmacies, care homes and other healthcare services, where appropriate to support patient care. Using practice and administrative systems, including EMIS, Docman and Microsoft Office . Full training will be provided where required. Supporting colleagues with general administrative duties and contributing to the smooth running of the practice. Assisting with the opening and closing of the practice when required. We are looking for someone who: Has excellent communication and interpersonal skills. Is friendly, approachable and professional. Has a strong commitment to providing excellent patient service. Is organised and able to prioritise competing demands. Can remain calm and professional when working in a busy environment. Has good attention to detail and is confident using computer systems. Is able to work effectively both independently and as part of a team. Is adaptable and willing to learn new systems and processes. Understands the importance of confidentiality and handling patient information appropriately. Previous experience within a GP practice, NHS or healthcare environment would be advantageous, but is not essential. This is an excellent opportunity to join a growing organisation where you will be part of a supportive team and have the opportunity to develop your skills and experience within primary care. If you are enthusiastic, organised and passionate about providing a high-quality service to patients, we would love to hear from you.

title: Medical Receptionist
description: Abbey Medical Centre Camden, London NW8 OAG. We are seeking committed receptionists, who demonstrate enthusiasm for working in primary care, with a genuine interest in working with patients and contributing to the delivery of high quality health care. Applicants should be courteous, highly motivated, pro-active and good team players, able to project a positive and friendly image to patients/visitors. These posts are full time/part time . Each of the posts available may be suitable for job share. Part Time will also be considered (over 5 days). This will involve working on reception (front desk), back office function including processing repeat prescriptions, scanning, summarising, filing medical records.etc. The job will be varied and time will be split between the roles. The surgery uses EMISWeb/DOCMAN 10 as their clinical system. The following are the core responsibilities of the receptionist/administrator. There may be on occasion, a requirement to carry out other tasks; this will be dependent upon factors such as workload and staffing levels: a. Maintaining and monitoring the practice appointment system b. Process personal, telephone and e-requests for appointments c. Answer incoming phone calls, transferring calls or dealing with the callers request appropriately d. Action all incoming faxes e. Signpost patients to the correct service f. Process incoming and outgoing mail g. Initiating contact with and responding to, requests from patients, team members and external agencies h. Process referrals to external agencies such as secondary care using the electronic referral system (ERS) i. Process calling letters are requested j. Process all DNA letters in accordance with current policy k. Action GP2GP tasks l. Read code data on EMIS Web m. Photocopy documentation as required n. File and store records as required o. Data entry of new and temporary registrations and relevant patient information as required p. Input data into the patients healthcare records as necessary q. Scanning of patient related documentation and attaching scanned documents to patients healthcare records r. Process requests for information i.e. SAR, insurance / solicitors letters and DVLA forms to the administrative team s. Manage all queries (including administrative queries) as necessary in an efficient manner t. Carry out system searches as requested u. Maintain a clean, tidy, effective working area at all times v. Monitor and maintain the reception area and notice boards w. Support all clinical staff with general tasks as requested Secondary Responsibilities In addition to the primary responsibilities, the medical administrator may be requested to: a. Partake in audit as directed by the audit lead b. Produce meeting agendas and record the minutes of meetings c. Support administrative and reception staff, providing cover during staff absences d. Complete opening and closing procedures in accordance with the duty rota e. As required support in the management of repeat prescriptions, ensuring they are processed accurately and efficiently f. Ordering and monitoring of stationery supplies

title: Medical Administrator
description: HAMPSTEAD GROUP PRACTICE (NW3 2QU) Medical Administrator Part-Time Post (25 - 30 hours per week) Hourly rate: £14.80 - £15.50 Working days: Monday - Friday We are seeking a motivated and reliable Administrator to join our busy and friendly team. The successful candidate will provide efficient administrative and secretarial support to the partners and clinical staff, ensuring high standards of service and patient care are maintained. The role involves managing clinical correspondence, processing referrals via the NHS e-Referral Service, and general administrative tasks. You will also process insurance forms, medical reports and medical record requests within agreed timescales, ensuring accurate record keeping and maintaining strict patient confidentiality. The ideal candidate will have excellent organisational skills, strong attention to detail and the ability to work both independently and as part of a team managing a varied workload in a fast-paced environment. Previous NHS or primary care experience and knowledge of EMIS are desirable but not essential. This is an excellent opportunity to join a supportive team within a well-established practice for a fixed-term maternity cover position. Provide administrative and secretarial support to GPs and clinical staff Preparation of medical correspondence Process patient referrals using the NHS e-Referral Service Manage insurance forms, medical reports and associated payments Process requests for copies of patient medical records Maintain accurate records and ensure documents are scanned into patient files Support cervical screening programme, QOF and flu campaigns Respond to patient and clinician queries relating to referrals and medical administration Provide occasional reception cover when required Manage workflow and coding Manage and action emails. Assist with Lab results. HAMPSTEAD GROUP PRACTICE Title: Medical Administrator Accountable to: Practice Manager Reports to: Practice Manager Liases with: Patients and Users of the Practice Professional Members of the Practice Team Patient Services Team and administrative staff PURPOSE AND OBJECTIVES OF THE ROLE To provide efficient and effective administrative and secretarial support to the partners and medical staff of the practice. The role involves coordinating a range of administrative processes and ensuring services are delivered within agreed quality standards and timeframes. KEY DUTIES AND RESPONSIBILITIES Secretarial and Administrative Support Provide efficient and effective secretarial support to partners and medical staff to an agreed quality standard and within agreed timeframes. Type all relevant practice correspondence as required, including Fit Notes requiring GP electronic signatures. Type medical reports as required. Record minutes of meetings when required. Provide administrative support such as photocopying, scanning and postal duties. Clinical Correspondence and Referrals Act as a first point of contact for doctors and patients with queries relating to medical matters and referrals. Process patient referrals promptly using the NHS e-Referral Service (eRS). Check the e-Referral Service system daily for rejected referrals and outstanding referral letters. Follow up queries relating to previously typed or submitted referrals. Deal with Advice and Guidance queries and responses. Maintain systems to ensure prompt processing of referrals and correspondence. Be responsible for two-week wait (urgent cancer referral) safety-net checks, ideally conducted weekly. Provide training to staff on the NHS e-Referral Service process when required. Medical Certification and Clinical Administration Send electronic copies of death certificates to Camden Registrars including patient next of kin details. Send cremation forms electronically to funeral directors and ensure copies are scanned into patient records. Process Telederm referrals including taking photographs of skin lesions and uploading them to EMIS records. Provide training to GPs on Telederm processes when required. Insurance Forms, Medical Reports and Claims Ensure that insurance forms, statutory claims forms and medical report requests are processed within 15 working days. Responsibilities include: Maintaining the insurance/claims and medical reports database. Logging all requests daily with the date received. Forwarding forms to the appropriate GP or partner for completion. Monitoring outstanding requests and following up incomplete forms. Ensuring completed documents are scanned and stored in the patients record. Dispatching completed documentation promptly to patients or requesting organisations. Processing income generated from these services and chasing outstanding payments. Distributing income received to salaried doctors where appropriate. Collating partner income and submitting records to the Business Manager and Finance Administrator for payroll processing. Subject Access Requests (Medical Records) Ensure requests for copies of medical records are processed within 28 working days. Logging all requests with the date of receipt. Preparing copies of paper and electronic records. Completing the initial check for third-party information. Passing records to a GP to check for third-party information. Ensuring redacted pages are scanned and appropriately coded in the patient record. Arranging secure transfer of records via recorded delivery, collection or encrypted email. Cervical Screening Administration Provide administrative support for the Cervical Screening Programme in accordance with national protocols. Inputting smear screening data into patient records. Monitoring and chasing outstanding smear results. Sending recall letters to non-responders. Processing Prior Notification Lists via Open Exeter within deadlines. Managing the colposcopy failsafe system. Supporting quarterly cervical screening targets as part of QoF and Enhanced Services. Medical Records Management Process urgent medical record requests and complete the appropriate request forms. Email urgent requests to PCSE and file copies within patient records. Follow up with PCSE if records are delayed. Ensure newly received records are reviewed by a GP and passed for summarisation if required. Document Management Undertake daily scanning of completed medical reports, insurance forms and related correspondence. Ensure scanning is completed in line with the Docman protocol. Additional Duties Maintain patient confidentiality and comply with information governance requirements. Maintain up-to-date contact records for affiliated organisations and services. Provide support to the management team when required. Assist with reception cover during staff shortages. Support practice activities such as the annual Flu Campaign and QOF targets. Undertake relevant training courses with agreement from the Practice Manager. Prepare refreshments for doctors coffee according to the rota. The Practice Manager will allocate duties, or the Business Manager in their absence. Duties may change to meet the operational needs of the practice. This job description is not exhaustive and may be amended by agreement between the Practice Manager and the post holder.
